title: Would a dedicated platform for AI-assisted games make sense?
author: Lightnig125
selftext:
Hey everyone,

With AI tools making game development more accessible, I've been wondering whether there's a need for a dedicated platform where developers can publish, share and potentially monetize games built with the help of AI.

Something similar to Steam or Itchio, but specifically designed for AI-assisted game development, with quality control to prevent AI slop and spam.

I'm curious about your experiences:

* Have you faced any difficulties publishing or promoting your AI-assisted games?
* Would you consider publishing your games on a dedicated platform?
* What would such a platform need to offer that Steam or Itchio doesn't already provide?

Would this solve a real problem, or is it simply unnecessary?

I'm currently exploring the idea and would love to hear your honest opinions, including criticism.

comments.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
comments.body:
If it’s something you want to start and maintain/run, I’ve already got a platform setup with license keys, a store etc and I could add an ai created category for you to manage as staff of that section. Let me know and we can chat and work something out

https://www.talkingpixels.games

replies.author: Lightnig125
replies.body: Thanks for the offer! But I was just asking out of curiosity, given how difficult it can be for some developers to release a game on Steam or Itchio without having it labelled as "AI slop."

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: Ya, that’s what I started expanding the tools I use for everyone after I looked into publishing and marketing lol. I’ve worked on the dev tools and engine for 5+ years and finally hitting soft launch.

comments.author: Icy_Potential_72
comments.body: Yes: Apple rejected my first game as "spam", and on Reddit people called it "AI slop" without trying it. But I'm not sure a separate store helps. Players care if a game is fun, not how it was made, and an "AI games" label might push them away.

replies.author: MelodramaticShape
replies.body: Buddy, I looked at your post history and the only people who crapped on your game was in a sub that is explicitly anti-AI. What did you expect to happen? Leave the persecution complex to people who actually need it.

replies.author: TechnicalCricket774
replies.body: Aw man I wanted to see his game but he privated his account🤣

replies.author: Icy_Potential_72
replies.body: You can play it right in Telegram, no install: search for LuckyStepGameBot and tap Play.

replies.author: Icy_Potential_72
replies.body: If you looked at my posts, you saw they're my first ones on Reddit. I'd just had the Apple rejection and was looking for answers, and I ended up in the wrong place for that. No complaints, lesson learned 🙂

replies.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
replies.body: Apple doesn't reject apps/games because of AI, spam means your app/game is 60% of your binary code or more is an exact copy of others on the store. Think solitare, solitare with cats, solitare with dogs, solitare with bats, you can develop it with assembly on a type writer and they would still reject it as spam (when it is)

comments.author: The-Iron-Ass
comments.body: If Epic couldn't pull people away from Steam despite giving millions in free games, what makes you think you can?

replies.author: Lightnig125
replies.body: I'm not planning to build a platform, I'm just asking out of curiosity. Some developers struggle to release their games on major platforms because of the backlash against AI. I'm just wondering if it's more about people's attitudes towards AI than anything else.

replies.author: Lightnig125

replies.author: Lightnig125
replies.body: Yeah, I understand that this would probably be the biggest challenge for such a platform. And that's exactly why [itch.io](http://itch.io) has had to remove some games labelled as "AI slop."

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body: I built one. It's its own engine. So quality control comes from the AI crawling the game before publishing to the site. It will also gather screenshots and make promotional videos for you. I will launch the feature soon. But check out the site if interested. [gengaming.net](http://gengaming.net)

comments.author: SquirrelinaboxMedia
comments.body:
There have been several dedicated platforms for AI assisted games posted on reddit.  They do not solve anything.  Somebody that built an AI game is looking for an audience, just like anybody else.  The problem is that creating a dedicated AI platform doesn't magically create an audience because nobody is specifically looking for AI assisted/created games (except for other developers).  

If an AI game has issues being called AI slop, then that's on the AI game, not the platform and a dedicated AI platform isn't going to help.  If a person doesn't want to play an AI game because it was built with AI assistance, then creating a dedicated platform for those types of games isn't going to get the anti AI crowd on board.  So in the end, a dedicated AI platform doesn't solve any of the issues you proposed.  

If somebody wants to create a game using AI, then they need to own it and just accept that there will be a portion of the population that won't like it.

replies.author: Lightnig125
replies.body: Yeah, that's a fair point! I agree with you. At the end of the day, a good developer can make a quality game regardless of whether they use AI or not.
